subject.title: Slack button interactions should dispatch a reply turn, not a heartbeat wake (follow-up to #99544)

question: Should Slack reply button/select clicks remain heartbeat-owned system events, or should the Slack plugin synthesize normal inbound reply turns for these user-initiated interactions?
rationale: Current source proves the mechanism is still heartbeat-based, but moving to inbound turns would replace a recently accepted system-event/heartbeat path and must preserve plugin interactive dispatch and approval early returns.

options.title: Move Reply Controls To Inbound Turns
options.body: Treat user-initiated Slack reply controls like normal channel input, with proof for clicked value delivery, Slack thread targeting, and busy-run coalescing.

options.title: Keep Heartbeat And Harden It
options.body: Retain the system-event heartbeat design only if maintainers require live proof and tests that interaction values visibly reply and survive active-session conflicts.

options.title: Wait For Live Proof
options.body: Keep the issue open without implementation until a current-main Slack trace proves the reply-drop or active-run loss beyond the source-level delivery-shape mismatch.

recommendation.title: Move Reply Controls To Inbound Turns
recommendation.body: Treat user-initiated Slack reply controls like normal channel input, with proof for clicked value delivery, Slack thread targeting, and busy-run coalescing.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available decision owner because the remaining choice crosses the core drain path and the linked predecessor closure evidence.
